answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity selling services such as inlet monitoring, pearl grading, or cedar pricing to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before accepting jobs. Bonds cannot be reused across identities or withdrawn early. Creating 10,000 fake agents therefore ties up $1 million for a month, even if none gets hired. The rule makes identities costly in proportion to their number, limiting how cheaply an attacker can flood the market.
